column4: The errand said only 'search the Iglesia del Cordon'. It had never been established that the registers were filmed, let alone transcribed.
column5: *** Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor is one of the most completely covered parishes this archive has touched *** - a near-unbroken run of a century, every volume in the full-text corpus. The Cordon is also where film 007713392 image 2511 sits, the cemetery act this archive already read to kill a false compound.

column4: The errand was raised expecting a volume or two to skim.
column5: *** THIS IS THE LARGEST UNWORKED SEAM IN THE ARCHIVE *** and it will not be done in an afternoon. *** Saying so is the point of this row: *** the errand stays OPEN with a real number against it instead of a vague instruction, because an errand that understates its own size is how a seam stays unopened for a month.

column2: a 'Juan Carlos' appearing beside the name in the Cordon results
column3: *** IT IS THE JUAN CARLOS GONZALEZ LERENA ALREADY HELD, AND HE IS NOT OURS ***
column4: A Juan Carlos anywhere near this surname has to be checked - it is the question the archive exists for.
column5: The snippet reads *** 'Blengio Gonzalez Lerena Juan Carlos con' *** - an index line, surname first. Run as a phrase it returns *** exactly one document, in Cordon Religious Marriage Records 1916-1926 *** - the man this register already carries as Juan Carlos GONZALEZ LERENA, married in the 1920s, a Gonzalez by his father and a Lerena by his mother. *** Our Juan Carlos fathered a child in 1882. Forty years and the wrong surname. ***
